keyJudgments.title: Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Agreement Reached in Washington
keyJudgments.description: After the fourth round of US-brokered talks at the State Department (June 2–3), Israel and Lebanon agreed to renew their fragile ceasefire and create 'pilot' security zones in southern Lebanon from which Hezbollah would be banned. The agreement is contingent on a complete cessation of Hezbollah fire and evacuation of all operatives south of the Litani River. Next talks scheduled for June 22.

keyJudgments.title: Hezbollah Rejects Ceasefire Terms, Continues Attacks
keyJudgments.description: Hezbollah Political Council member Mahmoud Qamati told the BBC: 'There was no ceasefire agreement.' The group insists it will not abide by any commitments made at the Washington talks, demands a complete halt to all Israeli operations and full IDF withdrawal from Lebanon. Hezbollah fired rockets at IDF troops in northern Israel on June 3 — the first such attack since June 1.

keyJudgments.title: Nine Killed in Southern Lebanon Airstrikes; 3,516 Dead Since March
keyJudgments.description: Israeli strikes hit approximately 20 locations across southern Lebanon on June 4, killing at least nine people including two paramedics whose ambulance was directly targeted in the Chehour area. A Lebanese army soldier was also killed near Nabatieh. Lebanon's health ministry has now recorded 3,516 deaths since the start of the war in March.

keyJudgments.title: IRGC Strikes Kuwait Airport; One Killed, 63 Injured
keyJudgments.description: Iranian IRGC drones struck Kuwait International Airport's Terminal 1 on June 4, killing one person and injuring at least 63 others. The attack followed US strikes on Qeshm Island after Iran targeted a blockade-violating tanker. Trump says US-Iran talks are going 'very well' and a deal could come 'over the weekend,' but Iran's FM says 'no tangible progress' has been made.

keyJudgments.title: IDF Deepens Southern Lebanon Ground Operation; No Ceasefire for Forces
keyJudgments.description: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir stated 'there is no ceasefire for our forces' in Lebanon on June 4. Golani Brigade held a command handover ceremony at Beaufort Castle — captured last Sunday — marking the IDF's deepest advance into Lebanon in 25 years. The IDF reports killing over 2,500 Hezbollah operatives since March, including hundreds from the elite Radwan Force.

keyJudgments.title: Lebanon Economy Faces 7–10% GDP Contraction; Reserves Draining
keyJudgments.description: Finance Minister Jaber projects the war could shrink Lebanon's GDP by 7–10% in 2026, with direct and indirect damage reaching $20 billion. Foreign reserves fell from $12.07B in mid-February to $11.43B by end of April — a $640M drain in 10 weeks. The Lebanese pound holds near 89,500 to the dollar but the stability is described as artificially managed.

items.heading: Fourth US-Brokered Trilateral Talks Produce Ceasefire Agreement
items.content: The US convened the fourth high-level trilateral meeting between Israeli and Lebanese representatives on June 2–3 at the State Department. The resulting joint statement announced agreement on ceasefire implementation contingent on Hezbollah's complete cessation of fire and evacuation from south of the Litani River. 'Pilot' security zones under exclusive Lebanese army control were agreed in principle. Next meeting set for June 22.

items.heading: Trump Confirms He Called Netanyahu 'Crazy' Over Lebanon Strikes
items.content: Trump confirmed he sharply criticized Netanyahu in an expletive-laden call, saying he was 'a little bit perturbed at his constantly fighting with Lebanon.' Trump said he told Netanyahu: 'Bibi, we've got to stop this.' Netanyahu acknowledged 'tactical disagreements' but said they 'always find a way to resolve them.' Trump is concerned Lebanon escalation could jeopardize a broader US-Iran deal.

items.heading: US House Passes Resolution to Halt Iran War
items.content: The US House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution to halt Trump's military campaign against Iran, with four Republicans joining Democrats. The vote is largely symbolic as the Senate would need to concur and Trump would veto. The vote reflects growing congressional opposition and is a public rebuke of the president's Iran policy.

items.heading: Iran Insists Lebanon Ceasefire Must Be Part of US Deal
items.content: Iranian FM Araghchi stated communications with the US remain open but 'no tangible progress' has been made. Iran continues to demand that any deal with the US include a complete halt to Israeli operations in Lebanon and full IDF withdrawal. Tehran warned that any attack on Beirut would trigger a 'full-scale resumption' of the war.

items.heading: OECD Cuts Global Growth Forecast Amid War Fallout
items.content: The OECD revised global growth downward to 2.8% if Gulf oil exports normalize in Q3, but warned growth could fall to 2.1% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027 if the war continues into next year. Oil prices eased on June 4 as the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement boosted hopes for a broader deal to end the West Asia war.

items.heading: IDF Strikes ~20 Locations in Southern Lebanon
items.content: Israeli forces struck approximately 20 locations across southern Lebanon on June 4, issuing evacuation warnings for several villages before attacks. Strikes hit the Nabatieh area, Chehour, al-Housh near Tyre, and a highway south of Beirut (Khaldeh). IDF Chief Zamir reiterated: 'There is no ceasefire for our forces' in Lebanon.

items.heading: Two Paramedics Killed in Ambulance Strike; Lebanese Army Soldier Killed
items.content: Two paramedics from the Risala Scouts Association (Amal-affiliated) were killed and a third seriously wounded when Israeli forces 'directly targeted' their ambulance in the Chehour area. Lebanon's health ministry accused Israel of 'contempt for international humanitarian law.' At least 128 healthcare workers have been killed in Israeli attacks since March. A Lebanese army soldier was also killed near Nabatieh.

items.heading: Hezbollah Fires Rockets at IDF Troops; Claims Beaufort Castle Drone
items.content: Hezbollah fired a 'salvo of rockets' at IDF soldiers in Qantara, southern Lebanon, and launched drones at troops near Beaufort Castle — the first attacks since June 1. Israel intercepted a drone and two projectiles. Hezbollah published FPV drone footage of the castle. IDF held a Golani Brigade command handover ceremony at Beaufort Castle, marking the deepest Israeli advance in 25 years.

items.heading: IDF Has Killed Over 2,500 Hezbollah Operatives Since March
items.content: The IDF reports killing over 2,500 Hezbollah operatives since March 2, including hundreds from the elite Radwan Force. Hezbollah has fired approximately 5,500 rockets at IDF troops in southern Lebanon and ~2,500 at Israel itself, with 75 rocket impact sites recorded in Israel. The IDF believes Hezbollah retains thousands of short-range rockets and hundreds of longer-range projectiles.

items.heading: Lebanese Army Denounces 'Pattern of Deliberate Strikes' on Its Forces
items.content: The Lebanese army said two of its soldiers were injured in a separate Israeli strike on their vehicle on the Deir Zahrani–Nabatieh road. The army denounced what it called 'a pattern of deliberate strikes targeting army personnel, vehicles and positions' by Israeli forces. The Lebanese army has been deploying to the Christian district of Tyre to demonstrate Hezbollah's absence.

items.heading: Lebanon Participates in Washington Talks; Rejects Foreign Hostage-Taking
items.content: Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh participated in the fourth round of US-mediated talks alongside Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter. The joint statement affirmed that 'the future of the relationship between Israel and Lebanon must be decided by the two sovereign governments' and rejected 'any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage' — a direct reference to Iran and Hezbollah.

items.heading: PM Salam Pushes Banking Reform Legislation Amid IMF Pressure
items.content: Prime Minister Nawaf Salam's government is attempting to advance draft legislation to address Lebanon's banking sector collapse, estimated at a financial deficit exceeding $70 billion. The IMF has called for comprehensive bank restructuring, a medium-term fiscal framework, and a debt treatment plan. Commercial banks, depositors, and independent economists all object to the current approach for different reasons.

items.heading: US Treasury Sanctions Lebanese Security Officials for Hezbollah Ties
items.content: The US Treasury Department recently sanctioned Brig. Gen. Khattar Nassereddine (head of security analysis, General Security Directorate) and Col. Samer Hamadeh (Army Intelligence) for allegedly leaking state intelligence to Hezbollah and obstructing disarmament. The Lebanese Army Command stressed its officers are loyal solely to the state. Political factions aligned with Hezbollah condemned the sanctions as 'political blackmail.'

items.heading: Lebanon Faces FATF Grey List Pressure; Finance Minister Warns of Black List Risk
items.content: Lebanon remains under increased FATF monitoring, placing pressure on correspondent banking relationships. Finance Minister Jaber warned: 'Lebanon has become a cash economy, and the real question is whether we want to stay on the grey list, or sleepwalk into a black list.' The Compliance Shield partnership between BDL, commercial banks, and Salim Khalil Financial Company is credited with reducing extreme exchange-rate fluctuations.

items.heading: Death Toll Reaches 3,516; Over One Million Displaced
items.content: Lebanon's health ministry reports 3,516 people killed by Israeli attacks since the war began in March. The UN reports more than one million people have registered as displaced. Israeli evacuation orders now cover more than one-eighth of Lebanese territory. The figures do not distinguish between combatants and civilians.

items.heading: Beirut Waterfront Displacement Camp: Thousands in Tents Without Basic Services
items.content: Thousands of displaced people are living in tents along Beirut's waterfront with limited access to food, clean water, and bathrooms. Resident Mariam Hessa (23) told the BBC: 'I want the ceasefire to be for all Lebanon, not just for an area like Dahieh or even the south. No, it's for all Lebanon. We need this.' Collective shelters in Tyre and Saida are reported full.

items.heading: 128 Healthcare Workers Killed; WFP Struggles to Deliver Aid
items.content: At least 128 paramedics and healthcare workers have been killed in Israeli attacks on ambulances and medical facilities since March. The World Food Programme is struggling to deliver aid amid ongoing bombardments. The health ministry accused Israel of demonstrating 'contempt for international humanitarian law' following the ambulance strike in Chehour.

items.heading: War Damage Estimated at $20 Billion; World Bank Reconstruction Needs at $11 Billion
items.content: Finance Minister Jaber projects total direct and indirect economic damage from the current conflict could reach $20 billion. The World Bank's assessment of the 2024 hostilities alone estimated $3.4 billion in physical damage, $5.1 billion in direct economic losses, and $11 billion in total recovery and reconstruction needs — costs that now compound with 2026 damage.

items.heading: IRGC Strikes Kuwait Airport; One Killed, 63 Injured
items.content: Iranian IRGC drones struck Kuwait International Airport's Terminal 1 on June 4, killing one person and injuring at least 63 others. Kuwait Airways resumed flights from Terminal 4 after severe damage to Terminal 1. Kuwait's Foreign Ministry said the country 'reserves the right to respond' and will 'neither accept nor tolerate' such attacks. The strike was retaliation for US strikes on Qeshm Island.

items.heading: US Strikes Qeshm Island After Iran Targets Blockade-Violating Tanker
items.content: US CENTCOM conducted self-defense strikes against drone ground control stations on Qeshm Island after Iranian forces launched attack drones at civilian ships in the Persian Gulf. US forces intercepted three drones. Iran also claimed anti-ship missile attacks on the Liberia-flagged MSC Panaya. The US previously disabled the Botswana-flagged M/T Lexie tanker transiting toward Iran's Kharg Island.

items.heading: Iran's Ghalibaf Takes Executive Role; Pezeshkian Reportedly Sidelined
items.content: Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf convened the Central Bank governor and key ministers to coordinate economic policy toward China — an unusual executive-level function for a parliament speaker. ISW-CTP assesses that President Pezeshkian has been sidelined, with IRGC officials gaining dominance. Ghalibaf's appointment as Special Representative for China Affairs on May 17 carries a different 'level of authority' than previous such roles.

items.heading: Iran Tries to Normalize Strait of Hormuz Control During Ceasefire
items.content: ISW-CTP assesses Iran is using the ceasefire period to normalize de facto control over the Strait of Hormuz. The US-sanctioned Persian Gulf Strait Authority continues posting data on ships requesting Iranian permission to transit. Iran is prioritizing 'legitimacy' of its sovereignty claims over toll collection. 85 Iranian parliamentarians called for ICBM development in a letter to Supreme Leader Khamenei.

items.heading: Saudi Arabia Conducts Intensive Contacts in Washington to Back Lebanon Talks
items.content: Al Jadeed reported intensive Saudi contacts in Washington aimed at securing the success of the Lebanon-Israel negotiations. Saudi Arabia's involvement signals Riyadh's interest in a stable Lebanon as part of broader Gulf normalisation dynamics. Qatar is also mediating in parallel with Washington talks.

outlook30Days.description: The June 4 ceasefire agreement is structurally fragile. Hezbollah has explicitly rejected its terms and continues to fire rockets and drones. Israel's military leadership has stated there is 'no ceasefire for our forces.' The next round of talks on June 22 will be critical, but the gap between Israeli demands (Hezbollah disarmament) and Hezbollah's demands (full IDF withdrawal) remains unbridgeable in the near term.

The IDF continues to expand its ground operation in southern Lebanon, now holding Beaufort Castle — the deepest advance in 25 years. With Hezbollah maintaining rocket and drone attacks, Israel is likely to continue pressing its military campaign regardless of diplomatic agreements. Further advances toward the Litani River cannot be ruled out.

Trump claims talks are going 'very well' and a deal could come 'over the weekend,' but Iran's FM says 'no tangible progress' has been made. Iran continues to link any deal to a halt of Israeli operations in Lebanon — a condition the US and Israel reject. The Gulf military exchanges (Qeshm strikes, Kuwait airport attack) risk derailing talks entirely.

With 3,516 dead, one million displaced, and evacuation orders covering one-eighth of the country, the humanitarian situation continues to worsen. Collective shelters are full, the WFP faces delivery constraints, and healthcare infrastructure is under sustained attack. No significant improvement is expected without a durable, comprehensive ceasefire.

Foreign reserves are draining at ~$64M per week. GDP contraction of 7–10% is projected for 2026. Banking reform legislation remains stalled. FATF grey-list pressure threatens correspondent banking relationships. The Lebanese pound's apparent stability masks deepening structural damage. Without a ceasefire and international reconstruction funding, the economic trajectory is sharply negative.

Iran's strikes on Kuwait airport signal willingness to attack Gulf states hosting US forces. The IRGC's normalization of Strait of Hormuz control and ongoing maritime harassment pose risks to global energy supply chains. If US-Iran talks collapse, a rapid escalation across multiple fronts — Lebanon, Gulf, Strait of Hormuz — is plausible within the 30-day window.
